history behavior.

**[3]** "Task Queues." *Temporal Documentation*, Temporal Technologies, Inc., n.d.
<https://docs.temporal.io/task-queue>
**Tier:** 2
Task queue architecture: three types (Activity, Workflow, Nexus), dynamic
allocation, polling model, persistence guarantees, default 4 partitions,
server-side throttling.

**[4]** "Child Workflows." *Temporal Documentation*, Temporal Technologies,
Inc., n.d.
<https://docs.temporal.io/child-workflows>
**Tier:** 2
Child workflow use cases, comparison with activities, ~1,000 child recommendation,
parent close policy, Continue-As-New interaction. Quote: "When in doubt, use
an Activity."

**[5]** "Continue-As-New." *Temporal Documentation*, Temporal Technologies,
Inc., n.d.
<https://docs.temporal.io/workflow-execution/continue-as-new>
**Tier:** 2
Continue-As-New mechanics: same Workflow ID, new Run ID, fresh event history,
Entity Workflow Pattern ("durable objects, not just processes"), "Continue-As-New
Suggested" signal, Execution Chain concept.

**[6]** "Workflow Execution Limits." *Temporal Documentation*, Temporal
Technologies, Inc., n.d.
<https://docs.temporal.io/workflow-execution/limits>
**Tier:** 2
Hard limits: 51,200 events or 50 MB. Warning: 10,240 events or 10 MB. Pending
operations: 2,000 each (activities, child workflows, signals, cancellations).
Nexus: 30 concurrent. Dynamic config keys for all limits.

**[7]** "Failures Reference." *Temporal Documentation*, Temporal Technologies,
Inc., n.d.
<https://docs.temporal.io/references/failures>
**Tier:** 2
Failure type hierarchy: ApplicationFailure ("the only type created by user
code"), ActivityFailure, ChildWorkflowFailure, TimeoutFailure, CancelledFailure,
TerminatedFailure. Propagation via cause field nesting. Workflow Task vs
Execution failure distinction.

**[8]** "Retry Policies." *Temporal Documentation*, Temporal Technologies,
Inc., n.d.
<https://docs.temporal.io/encyclopedia/retry-policies>
**Tier:** 2
Default retry parameters: Initial Interval 1s, Backoff Coefficient 2.0,
Maximum Interval 100s, Maximum Attempts unlimited. Formula:
min(InitialInterval × BackoffCoefficient^retry_count, MaximumInterval).
Activities retry by default; Workflows do not.

**[9]** "Detecting Activity Failures." *Temporal Documentation*, Temporal
Technologies, Inc., n.d.
<https://docs.temporal.io/encyclopedia/detecting-activity-failures>
**Tier:** 2
Four timeout types: Schedule-To-Start (∞, no retry), Start-To-Close (always
recommended), Schedule-To-Close (∞), Heartbeat. Heartbeat throttling formula:
min(heartbeatTimeout × 0.8, 60s). Cancellations delivered via heartbeat.

**[10]** "Persistence." *Temporal Documentation*, Temporal Technologies,
Inc., n.d.
<https://docs.temporal.io/temporal-service/persistence>
**Tier:** 2
Persistence as "the only required dependency." Four data types: Tasks,
Workflow Execution State (execution table + history table), Namespace Metadata,
Visibility Data. Supported databases: Cassandra v3.11/v4.0, PostgreSQL
13.18-16.6, MySQL v5.7/v8.0, SQLite v3.x (dev only).

**[18]** "Worker Performance." *Temporal Documentation*, Temporal Technologies,
Inc., n.d.
<https://docs.temporal.io/develop/worker-performance>
**Tier:** 2
Slot-based concurrency. Three suppliers: Fixed, Resource-Based, Custom.
Resource targets: CPU 0.8-0.9, Memory 0.5-0.8. Poller autoscaling recommended.
Metrics: worker_task_slots_*, schedule_to_start latency, backlog counts.
Eager Activity/Workflow Start features.

**[19]** "Python Interceptors." *Temporal Documentation*, Temporal Technologies,
Inc., n.d.

**Tier:** 2
Five interceptor categories: Outbound Client, Inbound Workflow, Outbound
Workflow, Inbound Activity, Outbound Activity. Chain architecture. Workflow
interceptors execute during replay — use is_read_only() to gate side effects.
Activity/Client interceptors unaffected by replay.

**[23]** "Failure Handling in Practice." *Temporal Blog*, Temporal Technologies,
Inc., n.d.
<https://temporal.io/blog/failure-handling-in-practice>
**Tier:** 3
Failure classification: where (platform/app) × when (transient/intermittent/
permanent). Non-retryable errors must be explicit. Anti-pattern: linear retry
(BackoffCoefficient 1.0). Forward vs backward recovery strategies.

**[24]** "Compensating Actions: Part of a Complete Breakfast with Sagas."
*Temporal Blog*, Temporal Technologies, Inc., n.d.
<https://temporal.io/blog/compensating-actions-part-of-a-complete-breakfast-with-sagas>
**Tier:** 3
Saga pattern: register compensations BEFORE forward operations. Compensations
must be idempotent. Java has built-in Saga class; Python/TS/Go use manual lists.
Anti-patterns: workflow-level timeouts (blocks compensation), termination
(prevents finally).

**[25]** "Activity Timeouts." *Temporal Blog*, Temporal Technologies, Inc., n.d.
<https://temporal.io/blog/activity-timeouts>
**Tier:** 3
Always set Start-To-Close. Without Schedule-To-Close, "Temporal retries for
up to 10 years." Heartbeat for activities >several hours. Schedule-To-Start
rarely needed, does not trigger retries.
